(Take care not to overcook it; it won’t brown, and it may still look slightly pink inside).","url":"https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024135-pork-bulgogi-with-spring-vegetables#recipe-step-4"},{"@type":"HowToStep","text":"Garnish with reserved scallions and sesame seeds, and serve hot over rice with reserved marinade for drizzling.","url":"https://cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024135-pork-bulgogi-with-spring-vegetables#recipe-step-5"}],"recipeYield":"4 servings","review":[{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Stacey"},"datePublished":"2026-08-27T13:15:24Z","reviewBody":"An enormous hit, and so, so easy!!! I love recipes that use pork tenderloin in new ways since it is such an economical protein."},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Jersey Jay"},"datePublished":"2026-07-26T15:58:23Z","reviewBody":"Subbed thin sliced sirloin beef for the pork and cut back on sugar and did half cup gojujang -  made a brighter sauce. Also subbed in glass noodles. Super easy and impressive meal!"},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Janey"},"datePublished":"2026-07-04T10:19:54Z","reviewBody":"@Sandy C. I had the same confusion (had downloaded the recipe some time ago).  I went back and looked on line and saw that the instructions now separate the marinade ingredients from the rest."},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Eric"},"datePublished":"2026-07-01T00:01:14Z","reviewBody":"Go low sodium soy sauce. I love a salty dish, but this was a bit intense with regular sit sauce."},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Lois"},"datePublished":"2026-07-01T00:01:13Z","reviewBody":"Ya'll... inferior gochujang is too salty (to make up for other flavor deficiencies...) which will lead to a saltier dish. Guaranteed this recipe was tested with superior ingredients. If you don't want to complain, buy better stuff."},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Laura"},"datePublished":"2026-06-29T00:05:42Z","reviewBody":"This was a big hit! I used 1/3 cup low sodium soy sauce + 1/6 cup water and followed the recipe for the rest of the marinade ingredients. Used veggies I had on hand: thinly sliced carrots, sugar snap peas and red onion. I think any combination of veggies would work here. Pork was incredibly tender and perfect after barely three minutes in the pan."},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"lizzysap"},"datePublished":"2026-06-25T11:36:35Z","reviewBody":"Made this with thin pieces of chicken and doubled the amount.  Very tasty but sauce became very watery in the pan.  Possibly b/c some of the chicken pieces were still slightly frozen.  Cooked mushrooms, scallions and bok choy ribs first and then removed from pan while I cooked chicken to prevent over cooking.  Then added everything back in.  One mistake was forgetting to reserve some of the marinade before I put the chicken into it - oops.  It still turned out great but will note for future!"},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Lynn T"},"datePublished":"2026-06-18T09:31:43Z","reviewBody":"Yumba! Satisfied our craving for gochujang. Pork is the star here. 
Excellent marinade. I put the tenderloin in the freezer for an hour before slicing. That helped."},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Meg"},"datePublished":"2026-06-16T08:38:22Z","reviewBody":"Used thinly sliced tofu as my partner doesn’t eat meat and it worked out wonderfully! I froze it first to give it a meatier texture, it fell apart a little bit cooking but that kind of worked out with the dish!"},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Rachel"},"datePublished":"2026-06-16T03:35:45Z","reviewBody":"This was fantastic. I followed the sauce recipe exactly using low sodium soy sauce and didn’t think it was too salty or sweet. Used 1.5 lbs pork loin that I put in the freezer for a bit for easier slicing. Did shredded carrots instead of radish. Will definitely make again!"},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Adding spice"},"datePublished":"2026-06-16T01:17:30Z","reviewBody":"Added chili crisp to the marinade for more of a kick and it was delicious!"},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Prep time much longer."},"datePublished":"2026-06-15T03:52:34Z","reviewBody":"Between slicing the meat and vegetables, fishing all the marinade ingredients out of the cupboard and measuring them, then mincing the garlic and ginger - 10 minutes prep time isn’t even close!"},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"chatulim9"},"datePublished":"2023-04-28T19:13:33Z","reviewBody":"be careful to purchase gochujang paste and not sauce.  Paste is used for cooking; sauce is used as an add-on at the table."},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Edith"},"datePublished":"2023-04-29T18:07:36Z","reviewBody":"I think cutting back on the sugar (while praiseworthy and well-intentioned) makes it taste more salty."},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"midwest cook"},"datePublished":"2023-04-24T12:40:19Z","reviewBody":"This was great, but a bit intense on the saltiness/sodium. Next time I'll use low sodium soy sauce. I also used shaved beef in place of the pork, about half the brown sugar and traded out sugar snap peas for the snow pea pods. Will definitely make this again."},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Ray"},"datePublished":"2025-05-04T00:18:35Z","reviewBody":"A reminder that cutting back on the sugar will also make the dish saltier (in asian cooking, sugar is often used with soy sauce to balance the strong salty flavor). If you have to cut the sugar, cut the soy sauce proportionately ... or just make another recipe."},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Volker"},"datePublished":"2023-05-02T14:25:36Z","reviewBody":"We really enjoyed this! Tons of flavor in the sauce/marinade and easy to pull together on a weeknight. A few tips: cook the mushrooms as directed, then add a 14 oz bag of frozen ‘stir fry veggies’ from the freezer aisle before you move on to cook the meat. Perfect balance of sauce, veggies, meat. I kept all other proportions consistent with the recipe and used low sodium soy sauce."},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Powell"},"datePublished":"2023-04-23T03:45:14Z","reviewBody":"Snow peas wilt very quickly.  Watch the time if you want them a bit crunchy."},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Mary"},"datePublished":"2025-04-28T15:48:06Z","reviewBody":"For those saying it’s salty (and I found it a bit soy forward) I enjoyed it with 1/3 cup soy topped up to 1/2 cup with water. As my large bottle of soy sauce ages it concentrates so I find dishes get saltier as I get closer to the bottom of my bottle.
This dish also worked with a mix of asparagus and snow peas instead of radishes for me. Use what you got."},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Mario B"},"datePublished":"2023-04-22T11:49:22Z","reviewBody":"Easy and delicious.  A bit of chopping involved which might not be ideal for a busy weeknight.  Used asparagus and peas."},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Tariqata"},"datePublished":"2023-04-29T03:06:20Z","reviewBody":"Delicious and easy! I used thinly sliced pork tenderloin, shiitakes and snap peas and really liked the radishes. Will be making this again."},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Kurt"},"datePublished":"2023-05-07T23:58:06Z","reviewBody":"Delicious! Followed the recipe except for subbing snap peas for snow peas. We thought it was excellent but a bit salty. I would probably only use 1/3 cup of soy next time, maybe even just 1/4 and have none reserved for drizzling, which we didn’t really feel we needed.  Once the marinading was done, it came together super quickly. Definitely a keeper."},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Kenneth Moon"},"datePublished":"2025-06-01T15:14:09Z","reviewBody":"This marinade/sauce is magical and will turn any pound of protein and 3 cups of veg into a delicious meal. Highly recommend sliced chicken tenders and 3 cups of broccoli, green beans and zucchini!"},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Robin Gausebeck"},"datePublished":"2026-02-12T22:03:38Z","reviewBody":"I've made this dish several times - fantastic. BUT...I make the marinade alone and use it for cold noodle salad, as a stir-fry sauce, as an accompaniment to Korean pancakes and mixed with some mayo for a sauce for shrimp. My husband likes the sauce so much he would probably just eat it with a spoon."},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Meredith"},"datePublished":"2026-04-11T12:47:44Z","reviewBody":"@Mario B have you tried the prepped veggie combo at Trader Joe’s? Asparagus, red onion and shiitake mushrooms. That might work well here."},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Betsy"},"datePublished":"2023-05-01T15:09:54Z","reviewBody":"We really enjoyed this - it was relatively easy and it was tasty. Can definitely add more veggies and could certainly sub the protein, but it's a great template for how to put together a bulgogi. Given the other comments I did use low sodium soy sauce and swapped the brown sugar for a little less honey."},{"@type":"Review","author":{"@type":"Person","name":"Lynne"},"datePublished":"2023-04-26T15:47:37Z","reviewBody":"Trader Joe's also carries it."}],"totalTime":"PT1H","url":"//cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024135-pork-bulgogi-with-spring-vegetables"}</script><script type="application/ld+json" data-next-head="">{"@context":"https://schema.org","@id":"//cooking.nytimes.com/recipes/1024135-pork-bulgogi-with-spring-vegetables","@type":"WebPage","author":{"@id":"nyt://person/5b6a0b7c-274c-584b-b151-4c6d3e0ca62f","@type":"Person","name":"Melissa Clark","url":"https://cooking.nytimes.com/author/melissa-clark"},"copyrightHolder":{"@id":"https://cooking.nytimes.com/#publisher","@type":"Organization","name":"NYT Cooking"},"copyrightYear":2023,"dateModified":"2025-05-28T00:00:00Z","datePublished":"2023-04-21T00:00:00Z","description":"In this easy recipe, a deeply flavored Korean bulgogi marinade is paired with sliced pork, which is seared in a skillet with snow peas, radishes and mushrooms. class="topnote_topnote__jH8tN"><div class="pantry--body topnote_topnoteParagraphs__A3OtF"><p class="pantry--body">In this easy recipe, a deeply flavored Korean bulgogi marinade is paired with sliced pork, which is seared in a skillet with snow peas, radishes and mushrooms. You can use the basic recipe as a template, substituting other proteins like chicken, tofu or, most traditionally, beef for the pork, and whatever quick-cooking vegetables you like: cherry tomatoes, zucchini, broccoli florets are all great options. Don’t worry about browning the pork here. The goal is to sear it long enough to just cook it through, while the sauce condenses and caramelizes, coating the meat and vegetables.</p></div><p class="topnote_relatedArticle__1O6C4"><span 1 teaspoon toasted sesame oil
2 cloves garlic, finely grated or minced
1 (2-inch) piece ginger, finely grated or minced
2 scallions, thinly sliced

4 ounces shiitake mushrooms, sliced (about 1 ½ cups)
½ cup thinly sliced radishes (about 5)
